title: Borneo Half Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Borneo Half Marathon Review: Course, Weather, Cut-offs, Prizes
meta_description: Borneo Half Marathon review from the 2026 race: a flat Kota Kinabalu course from Tanjung Aru to the City Mosque, 24°C at the 4.30am start, water every 2.5 km, a 3.5-hour cut-off, prizes five deep.
dek: What Kota Kinabalu's City Day half marathon was like to run in February 2026: the coastal course, the air before dawn, the water stations and cut-offs, the part-closed roads, and how fast you need to be to win a prize.
verdict: Enter if you want a flat, well-supported half marathon with a realistic shot at prize money. In 2026 the 21 km started at 4.30am from Padang Merdeka, ran from Tanjung Aru in the south to the City Mosque in the north on roads between about 8 m and 20 m above sea level, and had water and a medic every 2.5 km. The airport recorded 23°C to 24°C until 7.30am. Cash went five deep in eight age categories, and the tenth man ran 1:24:38. The catch is the roads and the entry window. Much of the route had only one lane closed, and the half marathon sold out within two weeks, so register early and run inside the cones.

sections.heading: The Course: Tanjung Aru to the City Mosque, Along the Coast
paragraphs: The 21 km starts and finishes at Padang Merdeka in the city centre and is really two out-and-backs [1]. Runners head south first, past Wisma Kewangan and the Federal Building along Jalan KK Lama, and turn at the Tanjung Aru Beach roundabout. The way back runs up the coast in a green lane past Gleneagles, Imago and the Marriott, then through the city on Jalan Coastal, Jalan Tun Razak and Jalan Haji Saman, past Wisma Merdeka, Suria Sabah and Jesselton Point [1].

The second half follows the sea north to the roundabout at the City Mosque, Masjid Bandaraya, and comes back the same way to Padang Merdeka [1]. It is a different route from the Borneo International Marathon's half marathon in May [2].

The course is flat. On the organiser's elevation profile it stays between about 8 m and 20 m, with two short rises to about 20 m, near km 2 and km 12.5 [1]. The route maps in the runner's guide carry the World Athletics and AIMS certified-course badge [3].

The 11 km is a single out-and-back north from Padang Merdeka along Jalan KK Bypass and Jalan Tun Fuad Stephens, past Tanjung Lipat and Taman Awam Teluk Likas, to a U-turn at Bulatan Pasir by the City Mosque; its profile sits at about 10 m, with only small bumps [4].

sections.heading: The Weather: 23°C to 24°C and Very Humid
paragraphs: Kota Kinabalu airport, about 5 km south-west of the start, recorded 24°C, a dew point of 22°C, 89% humidity and a 5-knot wind at the 4.30am start [5]. It then cooled slightly: 23°C with 88% to 94% humidity from 5.30am to 7am, when most half marathoners were on the course [5]. It was back to 24°C at 7.30am and 26°C with 79% humidity at the 8am cut-off [5].

A dew point of 22°C means sweat evaporates slowly, but with a light breeze and temperatures of 23°C to 24°C, the 2026 race was run in mild air for the tropics. A runner finishing inside three hours, by 7.30am, ran the whole way at 23°C to 24°C; the warm-up only came in the last half-hour before the cut-off [2][5].

sections.heading: Water Stations, Cut-offs and What Finishers Get
paragraphs: On the 21 km map there is a water station every 2.5 km, from Wisma Kewangan bus stop at 2.5 km to Tanjung Aru rugby field at 5 km, Wisma Perkeso at 7.5 km and the Marriott at 10 km, then JQ Central at 12.5 km and 20 km and Tanjung Lipat at 15 km and 17.5 km. Each one has a medic [1]. The 11 km has two stations at Tanjung Lipat, each passed on the way out and on the way back, at 1.7 km and 8.3 km and at 3.5 km and 6.5 km [4].

The cut-offs are strict: 3 hours 30 for the 21 km (8am) and 2 hours for the 11 km (7.30am), and runners outside them are swept back to the start [2]. Finishers inside the limit get a medal and an online certificate; only half-marathon finishers inside 3 hours 30 get the finisher tee. Every entrant gets an event tee and a goodie bag [2]. There were pacers for every 15 minutes from 1:45 to 3:30 [3].

sections.heading: The Roads: Mostly One Lane
paragraphs: Only the streets around the start were fully closed. City hall closed Jalan Dewan, Lorong Dewan and Jalan Padang from 4am to 8am on race day, and closed one lane at a time on Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman, Jalan Mat Salleh, Jalan Tun Fuad Stephens, Jalan Coastal, Jalan Tun Razak, Jalan Haji Saman and Jalan KK Bypass [6]. That covers much of the 21 km route [1], so for most of the race there is traffic in the next lane.
The 21 km flag-off was at 4.30am and the first finisher was expected at 5.45am [3]. With traffic in the next lane at that hour, stay inside the cones and wear something reflective.

sections.heading: Race Morning at Padang Merdeka
paragraphs: Half marathoners were asked to arrive at 3.30am, and 11 km runners at 4.40am [3]. City hall reported the mayor and the state assistant minister responsible for city hall flagging runners off at 5.30am; the programme shows that was the 11 km start, with the 21 km already an hour into its race [3][7]. The organiser's programme had the prize-giving at 7.15am and the bag drop closing at 8.30am [3].

There is no parking at Padang Merdeka itself, which city hall closed from 1am on the Friday to 9am on race day [6]. The runner's guide pointed runners to Gaya Street, Wisma Jubilee, Kampung Air, Bandaran and Sinsuran [3].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Arikchely Airyl Arikah won the 21 km in 1:18:59, from Azlan Kuste in 1:20:56 and Yannick Theriault in 1:21:16. Weiling Lai won the women's race in 1:31:02, ahead of Jing Jing Tiew in 1:36:35 and Hasnita binti Asis in 1:38:30 [8]. Tenth place was 1:24:38 for men and 1:46:25 for women [8]. The 11 km was won in 39:58 by Romieo Gomboh and in 49:06 by Sharlene Fioney Sonny [8].

Prize money is spread wide. In the 21 km, the top five in each of eight categories, open, junior veteran (31 to 40), veteran (41 to 50) and senior veteran (51 and over) for men and women, won RM1,300, RM800, RM500, RM300 and RM200; the 11 km paid RM600 down to RM100 [3][9]. Only finishers inside the cut-off qualify, and winners had to report to the winners' corner by 6.45am [3][2].

The age bands matter. The top three women were all in the 31 to 40 category, and a woman in the 51-and-over category was fifth overall in 1:42:50 [8]. On the 2026 results, a woman under 1:45 or a man under 1:25 had a real chance of a cash place in an age category.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: The 2026 race was run with city hall for Kota Kinabalu's 26th City Day, and drew more than 4,000 runners, with entrants from the UK, Hong Kong, Brunei, Singapore, the Philippines, the United States and Italy [7]. The organiser, the Kinabalu Running Club, said the half marathon sold out within two weeks of registration opening [3]. The 21 km cost RM120 to RM160 and the 11 km RM100 to RM130, depending on when you entered [10].

Race packs were collected at Dewan Serbaguna Masyarakat Luyang on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 February, 10am to 6pm, with a sports expo; no packs were issued on race morning [3][11]. Postage was offered within Malaysia only [2]. Entries cannot be refunded or transferred, you cannot change category, and bib swapping means disqualification [2].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a flat, fast half marathon in mild air for the tropics, with water every 2.5 km and a city holiday around it. It also suits age-group racers: with prizes five deep in four age bands for each sex, a good club runner has a chance at cash.
Think twice if you need closed roads, or if you would struggle to break 3 hours 30, which is enforced with a sweep.

The 2027 race is on Sunday 31 January, eight days earlier in the calendar, from Padang Merdeka [12][13]. The 21 km again starts at 4.30am with 3 hours 30, and the shorter race becomes a 10.5 km at 5.30am with 2 hours [14]. Entry fees for the 21 km are RM120 to RM190 and for the 10.5 km RM100 to RM150 [14]. Race packs are to be collected on 29 and 30 January, at a venue not yet announced, and the 2027 route maps had not been published; the site still showed the 2026 maps [14][15].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's runner's guide, route maps, race information and registration pages, city hall's reports, the results, and airport weather records.

faqs.question: What time does the Borneo Half Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Early. In 2026 the 21 km started at 4.30am and the 11 km at 5.30am, both from Padang Merdeka in Kota Kinabalu, and half marathoners were asked to arrive by 3.30am. The organiser has kept the same times for 31 January 2027, with the 21 km at 4.30am and the new 10.5 km at 5.30am.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off time at the Borneo Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Three and a half hours for the 21 km, which closed at 8am in 2026, and two hours for the shorter race, which closed at 7.30am. The organiser enforces it: runners outside the limit are swept back to the start and do not get the finisher medal, and only 21 km finishers inside it get the finisher tee.

faqs.question: How hot and humid is the Borneo Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Humid but mild for the tropics. At the 4.30am start in 2026, Kota Kinabalu airport recorded 24°C, a dew point of 22°C, 89% humidity and a 5-knot wind. It stayed at 23°C to 24°C until 7.30am, then rose to 26°C by the 8am cut-off, so a sub-three-hour runner avoided the heat.

faqs.question: Is the Borneo Half Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes. The organiser's 2026 elevation profile for the 21 km stays between about 8 m and 20 m, with two short rises near km 2 and km 12.5. The route runs south to Tanjung Aru and north along the coast to the City Mosque, with a water station and a medic every 2.5 km.

faqs.question: Are the roads closed for the Borneo Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Only partly. In 2026 city hall fully closed Jalan Dewan, Lorong Dewan and Jalan Padang around the start from 4am to 8am, but closed only one lane on the main roads of the route, including Jalan Tun Fuad Stephens, Jalan Coastal and Jalan Tun Razak. Expect traffic beside you.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to win a prize at the Borneo Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not elite fast. In 2026 the 21 km paid the top five in each of eight age categories, from RM1,300 down to RM200. The men's race was won in 1:18:59 and tenth place was 1:24:38; the women's winner ran 1:31:02 and tenth was 1:46:25. Winners must finish inside the cut-off.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the previous edition (8 February 2026). Built mainly from the organiser's 2026 runner's guide and route maps, the registration pages, city hall's reports, the published top ten and airport METAR observations. City hall says the flag-off was at 5.30am; the organiser's programme shows that was the 11 km start with the dignitaries, and the 21 km went at 4.30am. The Daily Express report was behind a bot check and full results were blocked, so no finisher count or press figures beyond city hall's are used. No runner accounts of the 2026 race could be found. No rating.
